member.name: T:HaulBuilder.ClusterHauling
member.summary: Cluster hauling after the flow ribbon hands off. Each pass clusters the current residual, pairs it, and runs at most ten trips. The old schedule is then dropped and the field is clustered again. Hauling stops when a plan has no trips, which hands off to thin-cut. Five hundred trips is a planner error: the search stops and does not enter thin-cut. The 50 mm band is not the switch. Cells are cut and filled to the target.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ClusterHauling.NO_HAULABLE_WORK
member.summary: Normal end. The current residual scheduled nothing.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ClusterHauling.TRIP_LIMIT
member.summary: Error end. The same work kept coming back. Correcting does not start.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ClusterHauling.PICTURE_STOP
member.summary: Early stop for a picture of the first routes. Thin-cut does not start. The production loop does not use this reason.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ClusterHauling.MAX_CLUSTER_TRIPS
member.summary: Executed cluster trips before the search treats the planner as stuck.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ClusterHauling.TRIPS_PER_PLAN
member.summary: Trips driven from one schedule before the field is clustered again.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ClusterHauling.CANDIDATE_PAIRS

member.name: T:HaulBuilder.Correcting
member.summary: Coverage passes after thin-cut. This is the last stage. Lines run the length of the field along the mean flow, a pan width apart, as a serpentine, then a headland lap parallel to the boundary. The blade is at the target. High cells fill the bowl and low cells take a spread lift. The field's imbalance is a sink or a source on cells at the target, used only when the current line and the next line have no real destination or source. A leftover load is hauled to a low, and that trip is part of the distance. Coverages repeat while the planing gate fails and the last coverage reduced the haul error by at least one percent.

member.name: T:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch
member.summary: Builds each load from the crossover, where remaining cut meets fill. The search works backwards along the Poisson flow. That line is the priority. Once no arrow still fills a bowl, the blade may leave the arrow by 10 percent, and that cone opens in the same steps while a full bowl can still be made. Where a flow line cannot be followed, the ground is a ridge, and the cut follows the ridge only while that soil still drains back through this mouth. Soil that runs to another fill is another load. The fill follows the flow on into the basin. Cells already at grade are driven across with the blade grading, and the dirt stays in the bowl until the next cell that is still low. Once that still cannot fill a bowl, the fill may cross a small leftover ridge and place the rest of the bowl in the basin the arrow reaches. The haul is still only the gap to the first of those low cells. As the field is levelled the crossover moves and the finished band between cut and fill gets wider. Turning-circle guidance then drives the path. The search is a state machine. When the cluster window is on, each trip is the cheapest seconds per yard among the next flow trip, the cluster plan, and the thin-cut plan. Hauling stops when none of those is under the ceiling, and correcting starts. A window of zero keeps the flow ribbon.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.TRACE_STEP_CELLS
member.summary: Step along the streamline, in cells. Short enough to visit every cell.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.MISS_GAP
member.summary: Empty steps in a row that end a ribbon.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.MAX_TRACE_STEPS
member.summary: Steps before a trace gives up. Stops a loop on a flat arrow.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.SMOOTH_PASSES
member.summary: Neighbor averages applied to the arrow field so the ribbon steers smoothly.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.MATCH_TOLERANCE_BCY
member.summary: Cut and fill on one load must match tighter than the ledger check.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.MAX_STRIPS
member.summary: Strips one load may take. A full bowl can be several trips back to dirt that was not beside the first strip.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.MAX_STRIP_TRIES
member.summary: Seeds tried while filling one bowl. A seed that grows nothing is skipped.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.ADJACENT_CELLS
member.summary: How far, in cells, the next cut strip may sit from dirt already on this load. A turnaround across this gap is shorter than hauling a half-empty bowl.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.FILL_REACH_CELLS
member.summary: Fill may be gathered anywhere still open. The machine is already going there to dump, and a full bowl saves the return trip.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.FULL_BOWL
member.summary: Fraction of scraper capacity each load takes before it hauls. The bowl is filled even when the next strip means driving back.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.MIN_CELL_COVERAGE
member.summary: Minimum share of a cell the blade must cover before the cell is cut or filled. The blade is one cell wide. On a diagonal it covers about a quarter of each cell beside the corner, and those cells are the continuous strip. A cell below this share was only nicked, and taking it paints a splotch.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.COVERAGE_SAMPLES
member.summary: Samples along each cell edge when measuring how much of it the blade covers.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.COVERAGE_SAMPLE_REACH_CELLS
member.summary: Distance, in cells, from a cell center to the farthest coverage sample. Samples sit half a step in from the edge, so the true corner is (0.5 - 0.5/8) * sqrt(2), about 0.619. A hair past that corner keeps a borderline cell on the sample grid. A center closer than the blade minus this reach is fully covered, and a center farther than the blade plus this reach covers nothing.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.FlowRibbonSearch.FORWARD_DOT
member.summary: Minimum alignment of a step with the flow. About 32 degrees. A wider step leaves the streamline and fills the pocket as a blob.

member.summary: Gathers one blade-wide ribbon from the crossover. Sign -1 follows the Poisson flow up the slope. Sign +1 follows it into the fill. A fill keeps going across cells already at grade. Where that line ends, a cut follows the ridge only while the soil drains back through the mouth. A fill eases along the valley.
member.param: Cell the ribbon must pass through.
Depth still available. Reduced by what this ribbon takes.
Bank cubic yards per metre of depth.
Volume this ribbon may still take.
Deepest one pass may take from one cell.
Fill centroid the ribbon steers toward.
Cells on the outer boundary, where a sharp turn is a headland.
When true, finished cells do not end the ribbon. The blade stays down and the dirt stays in the bowl until the next low cell. A cut passes false, so running out of soil still ends that strip.
Cut still to take. While dragging, a cell that still needs cutting is not finished grade, and the fill stops there.
Cells already on this load. A second layer is not taken.
Tightest blade-down radius, in metres. The field edge may use it. A bend inside the cut or the fill uses a wider radius.
Fraction of the arrow a step may leave. Zero follows the arrow.
When true, a fill keeps going across a short leftover ridge. The high cells are left for a later cut.
member.returns: Cells in drive order. Upstream growth is reversed so the seed is last.

member.summary: Walks downstream from the cut mouth along the flow until fill remains, then takes a blade-wide ribbon of that fill up to the cut volume. The fill is the basin that flow reaches. Cells already at grade are graded across, so a later low cell on the same flow still receives dirt. The haul stays the gap to the first low cell.
member.param: Bank cubic yards per metre of fill depth.
Cut volume that must be matched.
Deepest one pass may take from one cell.
Fill centroid the ribbon steers toward.
When true, a fill that comes back beside its start is kept. That is only the end of the field, after every straight strip is gone.
Cells on the outer boundary, where a sharp turn is a headland.
Cut still to take. The fill stops on that ground.
Tightest blade-down radius, in metres. The field edge may use it. A bend inside the fill uses a wider radius.
Fraction of the arrow the walk may leave. Zero follows the arrow.
When true, the fill keeps going across a short leftover ridge and places the rest of the bowl in the basin beyond it.
member.returns: Fill cells in drive order, nearest the cut first.

Manual assists break ties only, because their length is already inside that score. Equal scores keep the earlier seed.

member.name: T:HaulBuilder.HaulCostSearch
member.summary: At each haul, prices the next flow trip against the best trip in the current cluster plan and the best trip in the current thin-cut plan. The cheapest seconds per bank cubic yard is kept. A plan refreshes after ten trips from that stage. A batch that no longer fits is replaced from the rest of that plan, and a used-up plan refreshes on the same ten-trip cadence.

member.name: T:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions

member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum routes pooled in one consolidation transaction.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.RouteConsolidationMaximumCycles
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum cycles removed by consolidation.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.PairRefinementRounds
member.summary: Gets or sets deterministic equal-load fill-pair refinement rounds. A ribbon plan keeps the passes the search built. Zero skips refinement on every other plan.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.EnableMultiRouteExchange
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the slower closed multi-route exchange runs.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.MultiRouteExchangeRounds
member.summary: Gets or sets bounded multi-route exchange rounds.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.MultiRouteExchangeGroupSize
member.summary: Gets or sets maximum routes in one multi-route exchange.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.MultiRouteExchangeMaximumGroups
member.summary: Gets or sets maximum committed multi-route exchanges.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.MultiRouteExchangeMinimumImprovementM
member.summary: Gets or sets minimum compact-guidance improvement per exchange.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.EnableCycleChainOptimization
P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.CycleChainRounds
member.summary: Gets or sets field-wide fill-chain rounds.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.CycleChainCandidatesPerRoute
member.summary: Gets or sets exact candidates checked per route.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.CycleChainMinimumImprovementSeconds
member.summary: Gets or sets minimum production-objective saving per chain exchange.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.RouteReorderWindow
member.summary: Gets or sets route relocation search window; zero disables relocation.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.EnableEarlyFullStripBanding
member.summary: Gets or sets whether routes are driven as one-strip interior loads, then other interior loads, then the field-edge batch. The reorder window stays inside a band. On by default. Off is one travel sort of every load.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.OptimizeRouteOrderByDistance
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the next load is chosen by metres. The score is the empty hop plus the turn arc. On by default. Off scores the same hop in seconds, with the turn at turn speed.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.ClusterModeAverageWindow
member.summary: Gets or sets whether hauling prices each trip by seconds per yard. A positive window, with a positive fraction, compares the next flow trip with the cluster plan and the thin-cut plan. Zero keeps the flow ribbon for the whole field. The count is no longer a mean.

member.name: P:HaulBuilder.HaulOptimizationOptions.ClusterModeLoadFraction
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the cost selection is allowed to leave the flow ribbon. Zero keeps hauling on the ribbon. The default is one half, which leaves it on.

member.summary: Copies all resolved tuning values.

member.name: T:HaulBuilder.ResidualClusters
member.summary: Groups residual cut and fill into clusters. It does not pair them or plan a route. A cell more than seeds a cluster. The cluster grows through cells more than , then across a gap of . Volume above the floor must reach half a bowl or the component is dropped. A cluster bigger than bowls is bisected along its long axis until every piece is within that limit. Clusters are the reporting regions. Pieces are the parts a later step can pair.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ResidualClusters.DEEP_MM
member.summary: Depth, in millimetres, that can seed a cluster.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ResidualClusters.FLOOR_MM
member.summary: Depth, in millimetres, through which a seed may grow. Volume is counted above this.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ResidualClusters.GAP_CELLS
member.summary: Gaps this many cells wide are bridged into the cluster. Bridged cells add no volume at or below the floor.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ResidualClusters.CONNECTIVITY
member.summary: Neighbourhood used for the seed grow, the gap bridge, and the component labels.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ResidualClusters.MIN_CLUSTER_BOWL_FRACTION
member.summary: Share of the bowl a cluster must hold, measured above the floor.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ResidualClusters.MAX_PIECE_BOWLS
member.summary: A piece larger than this many bowls is bisected along its long axis.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ResidualClusters.MEDIAN_SLACK
member.summary: Relative slack when the running haul meets half a piece. A rounding error must not pull another cell across the median.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ResidualClusters.M3_TO_CY
member.summary: Cubic metres to cubic yards. Specified as 1.30795.

member.name: M:HaulBuilder.ResidualClusters.Build(System.Double[0:,0:],System.Boolean[0:,0:],System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Clusters the residual grid.
member.param: Residual in millimetres. Positive is cut. Negative is fill. Indexed [row, col].

member.returns: The kept clusters, the pieces cut from them, and the diagnostic counts.

member.name: T:HaulBuilder.ResidualHauls
member.summary: Builds one loaded haul for each scheduled cluster or thin-cut trip. A trip cuts the highest cells of one piece and fills the lowest cells of the paired piece. One cut takes at most 61 mm and stops at the target. One fill cell takes at most one spread and stops at the target. The next piece is used only when the larger one has nothing left above target. The haul is the straight line from the cut piece's exit face to the fill piece's entry face.

member.name: F:HaulBuilder.ResidualHauls.BLADE_M
member.summary: Blade width used to stripe a piece. One shop cell is one blade.
Allocates cells and plans a haul for every trip, in schedule order. A later trip can take the next lift of a cell this trip did not finish.
member.param: Residual in millimetres, indexed [row, col]. Positive is cut.
Pieces that were paired, including their cells.
Field grid. Cell centres and the picture use this.
Bank yards of fill per loose yard. Clustering's compaction.
Grade tolerance in millimetres. A hauled cell is left within this of the target.
Smoothed flow east. The heading is the paired fill, not this arrow.
Smoothed flow north. The heading is the paired fill, not this arrow.
Pan capacity. A trip payload above this is cut down to one bowl.
member.returns: One haul per trip, in the same order.

member.summary: Retries an otherwise infeasible exact sequence with bounded work-end retreats. A retreated endpoint starts or finishes its connector directly at the work point, allowing the turn to begin before a field edge while recording the resulting nominal coverage shortfall.

member.name: M:HaulBuilder.RunSequencer.SelectBoundedFlexibleOptions(System.Collections.Generic.List{HaulBuilder.RunSequencer.SequencedRun},System.Double)
member.summary: Retains low-cost flexible variants plus the deepest entry, exit, and combined retreats so bounded search does not discard edge clearance.

Builds a deterministic bounded flexible-endpoint sequence when subset search would grow exponentially. A small number of alternate first choices is tried only when the default greedy walk cannot finish.
Keeps only a fixed number of lowest-cost partial flexible sequences at each depth, preventing subset-state growth while avoiding greedy traps.

Exhaustively orders the already-pruned flexible endpoint options for a small run group. Connector costs are cached by endpoint pair, so the exponential portion is limited to at most 2^10 subset states rather than repeatedly invoking the geometric planner for every ordering.

Tries a bounded nearest-first set of forward-only transitions from runs which have no ordinary outbound edge. Successful costs are fed into a second exact-order pass; normal runs never pay for this search.
Builds one bounded greedy flexible order.

member.name: T:HaulBuilder.StripLanes
member.summary: Area placement for one cluster or thin-cut trip. The piece is split into bands parallel to the haul heading, one blade wide. The fullest band is taken first. Inside a cut band the highest cells go first, and inside a fill band the lowest cells go first. A cell moves only when its band is chosen. The time is the sum of the chosen band lengths over the ground that moved, plus a loop between bands. The haul is from the cut piece's exit face to the fill piece's entry face.

member.summary: Thin-cut after cluster hauling stops. Cut and fill both come from square tiles on mask E. A cut tile is the soil above 10 mm. A fill tile is the hole below −30 mm, taken all the way to the target. Pairing, merging, and the trip schedule are the cluster steps. The loop replans every ten trips and stops when a fresh plan has no trips.

member.name: M:HaulBuilder.TransitPlanner.IsGrosslyDisproportionate(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Rejects exact-pose geometry whose distance is grossly out of proportion to an already validated small-angle forward alternative.
member.remarks: The multiplicative 4× gate catches tiny near-coincident loops. The half-turn waste gate catches full-circle Dubins words on longer corridor jogs (e.g. TheShop2 route 7 fill→fill) where 2πR is only ~2–3× the straight jog and would otherwise survive the 4× test.

member.name: M:HaulBuilder.TransitPlanner.ShortAlignmentJog(HaulBuilder.ConnectorPlanner.Pose,HaulBuilder.ConnectorPlanner.Pose,System.Double,HaulBuilder.Grid)
member.summary: Uses a short forward jog when two nearby poses differ only by the small endpoint correction intentionally delegated to guidance/operator tracking. This prevents an exact-pose Dubins solution from inserting a full loop to resolve a few degrees across approximately one blade width.
member.remarks: Tolerance is 30° (not 15°) so a short corridor right-jog whose chord bears slightly off the travel heading still qualifies — TheShop2 route 7's fill→fill connector was ~28° off and otherwise fell through to a 2πR loop.

member.name: T:HaulBuilder.TripGuidance
member.summary: Guidance between the blade-down lanes the planner already chose. Each trip may reverse a spread lane, and a cut lane when the lane is flat. A lane end within a turning radius of the boundary may bend on a blade-down quarter circle so the turnaround stays in the field. A forward Dubins connector joins the chosen shapes. The loaded connector from the cut end to the spread start is part of that score. Lane direction is chosen by time alone. A short joint is a straight steer across, or a trimmed lane, instead of a loop. A grade pass then runs back over the fill. A correcting trip does not grade: the land plane follows. Its lines are one sweep, at most three cut lines and three spread lines, and the spreads snake. A correcting line starts at its first fragment and ends at its last, so the connector owns the turn. A connector is chosen from the six Dubins words and the short-joint trims. Within two percent of the shortest, or half a radius when that is more, the path with the least length outside the field wins. A clearly shorter outside path is kept. Two connectors with no lane between them become one Dubins path. A short correcting trip may merge into a later correcting trip whose route passes within two radii. An end fragment of a correcting line that is shorter than one radius, and more than four radii past the next fragment, is deferred. After correcting, sweep-up trips take that pool by nearest neighbour until the bowl is full, then use the same correcting shape. A cut or spread shorter than half a radius, or lighter than one percent of the bowl, does not separate connectors. Its cells are still cut and filled. After every trip is fixed, trips are reordered inside their own stage to shorten the empty returns. Two trips that share a cell keep their order.

member.summary: Picks lane directions and boundary bends for one trip. Every spread lane may face either way. A cut lane may face either way only when it is flat; a slope keeps the downhill direction. An end within a radius of the boundary may also bend left or right. At most four lanes on each side are tried, and at most 256 combinations. The winner is the least time. That time includes the loaded connector from the last cut to the first spread, at the connector's real length. An equal time keeps the earlier combination, which is the planned lane. Outside connectors are counted in the report and do not decide the direction. A correcting trip gathers fragments that share a line, visits each line once in offset order, and keeps at most three cut lines and three spread lines. Spread lines snake. Those lines are clipped to their fragments and are not bent out to the field edge. A short end fragment more than four radii past the next fragment is deferred for a sweep-up trip. A flat solo cut may still reverse.
member.param: Cut lanes in the planner's drive order.
Spread lanes in the planner's drive order.
Next trip's first cut. Null after the last trip.
Field grid. Existing elevation is the loading slope.
Field test. Null does not test the field.
Blade width. The bend keeps the band's outer edge on the boundary.
Cell area. Zero skips the light-lane volume test.
Bowl capacity. Zero skips the light-lane volume test.
True defers a short isolated end fragment. Sweep-up trips pass false.
Dubins rules. Null uses the production defaults, or the rules of the build that called this.
member.returns: The chosen lanes and the course they drive.
